title: Linking, Routing and Fairness for Through-Year Assessment
text: occasions’ true scores (interims reporting scales, summative) jointly multivariate normal. Observed scores add known measurement error, score may missing. EM uses SQUAREM acceleration E-step batched missingness pattern, makes fast even though interim true scores correlate around 0.99. student’s summative prior conditional distribution given interims, measurement error carries forward late enrollers get wider priors rather wrong ones.

title: Linking, Routing and Fairness for Through-Year Assessment
text: 3,000 calibration 3,000 operational students; 3 interims; 10% late enrollers missing 2 interims; 10% “fast growers” gain +0.6 logits last interim. Priors calibrated: z mean 0.02, SD 0.99, 90% intervals cover 90.5%. Late enrollers get wider priors (0.45 vs 0.35) still calibrated (coverage 91%). Latent correlations recovered within 0.01. Policies (1-3 MST): Fairness one-directional: Scoring interim prior penalizes students whose growth accelerated last interim. Using prior routing keeps reported scores unbiased. conventional population prior bias: -reports lowest scorers. Routing priors send fast growers easier modules often (28% vs 15%), costs precision bias. Summative replacement (proficiency cut theta = 0.3): Overall accuracy -year replacement looks good summative’s, misclassifies late bloomers nearly four times rate. defensibility question accountability.

title: Linking, Routing and Fairness for Through-Year Assessment
text: Done: ty_simulate, ty_link (+predict), ty_mst, ty_mst_default, ty_administer, ty_policies, ty_fairness, ty_decisions. Rasch MST; linear growth simulator (linking distribution-free beyond multivariate normality). Next: growth-aware links (occasion timing covariate), adaptive shrinkage prior (discounting interim evidence stale), subgroup-calibrated priors, 1-2-3 panel designs.
